transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-10
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Marta (NovaChat CTO), Priya (Infra), Liam (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC throughput tuning; reviewed last week's benchmark numbers, discussed continuous batching and concurrency targets, queueing/backpressure strategies, and next steps to run a larger stress benchmark. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Last week's perf numbers (p95/p99, tokens/sec)
- Continuous batching parameters and tradeoffs
- Concurrency per-GPU vs global queuing
- Fallbacks and queue time SLOs
- Next benchmark plan and logging artifacts to collect

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Um, real short agenda: review the numbers you sent, Samira has a recommended config, we wanna nail down concurrency targets and queueing behavior before the bigger run.
[00:18] Marta: Yeah thanks Jordan, we heard back from legal last night, but that's a separate thread. Today it's really about whether we can hit the 10k qps target for our short prompts with p95 under 180ms.
[00:32] Samira: Cool, so quick recap - last week's run on your staging cluster, NovaChat-stg, single region, 4x A100 equiv, you were getting ~3.2k effective qps at steady state, tokens/sec about 240k, p95 around 230ms, p99 spiked to 610ms during burst periods. Note transcription may say A-100s as a one zero zero, sigh.
[00:53] Priya: Yep that's consistent with our dashboard. The big issue is tail latency during burst windows when request concurrency jumps. We saw queue depth spike and GPU utilization drop briefly while the scheduler rebalanced.
[01:10] Jordan: Right - so couple things Samira recommended: increase continuous batch window to 30ms from 10ms, bump max_batch_size to 256 for the model family you're running, and set per-device concurrency cap to 12 to avoid head-of-line blocking. That got you from 3.2k to about 4.5k in Samira's lab runs.
[01:36] Liam: Sorry can I clarify, when you say continuous batching window you mean the runtime holds open the KV cache to collect incoming tokens for up to that window before dispatch, right?
[01:45] Samira: Yeah exactly, it's a small latency add but increases batch depth so throughput goes up. The tradeoff is your latency SLO - if your p50 target is strict, we tune differently. For NovaChat you said p95 <= 180ms, so 30ms window seemed acceptable in the lab.
[02:03] Marta: Our user flows are short, median tokens per request is 45 and about 60% of requests are sub-50 tokens. We care a lot about p95 for interactive feel.
[02:14] Jordan: Good to know. Another lever is quantized model variant; Samira ran int8 quant on similar model and saw 20-30% token throughput uplift with modest quality delta. Would that be acceptable for a canary?
[02:27] Priya: Potentially, but need to run A/B on quality. Also we need to confirm keys and KMS behavior in Private deployment; last week you mentioned KMS integration steps.
[02:37] Samira: Yep I'll attach the KMS integration note in the shared folder.

[02:50] Samira: On concurrency vs global queueing - we recommend per-GPU soft caps plus a small global queue with backpressure. For your workload we suggested per-device concurrency 10-12, global inflight queue cap at 600 requests, and a SLO-based admission controller that drops or routes to a cheaper model at 800+ queue depth. In our tests that flattened p99 spikes.
[03:18] Liam: The 600 number - is that for the whole cluster or per-region?
[03:23] Samira: Whole cluster for the staging region you ran. If you go multi-region we'd partition.
[03:28] Jordan: Also important: request shaping. If you can add a fast pre-check to classify short vs long prompts we can route short ones to a low-latency path with aggressive batching. We briefly talked about that in the doc.

[03:45] Marta: Can you share the raw benchmark scripts and the logs so our SREs can replay?
[03:50] Samira: Absolutely - I'll push the script and a small ingestion manifest to the shared drive. We'll include perf counters, GPU traces, and the runtime trace of batching events (note sometimes the trace label says KV cash instead of KV cache in auto transcribed notes).

[04:10] Jordan: I pulled the bench results you uploaded - I noticed the p99 spike correlated with a drop in batch depth around the 14:32 window, looks like a rebalance event. Samira, what causes that?
[04:22] Samira: Typically imbalance happens when a burst of tiny requests arrives skewed to one node or when the KV caches aren't warmed. Two fixes: warm the caches with synthetic prefixes and/or enable cross-device prefetching so hot KV pages are available. Also tune the scheduler's rebalance threshold from 0.2 to 0.05 in your config to be less aggressive.
[04:44] Priya: Warm-up sounds straightforward. How long of a warm window do you recommend?
[04:48] Samira: We usually do a 3-5 minute warm-up before the full run; for your prompt mix 3 minutes was enough in our lab.

[05:05] Liam: For concurrency, you suggested cap 12 per device. How many devices do we have in staging?
[05:10] Priya: Right now staging is 4 GPUs per node x 6 nodes, so 24 GPUs total.
[05:16] Jordan: So at cap 12 that's 288 concurrency overall; with batching that maps to, roughly speaking, 5-6k qps for your short prompt mix, assuming batch depth of ~160. That's aligned with the lab numbers.

[05:34] Marta: What about autoscaling during peaks? We can't afford huge overprovisioning on cost.
[05:39] Samira: We recommend target-based autoscale using token/sec and queue depth as triggers. For example scale-up when queue depth > 500 for 30s and scale-down after 3m of low load. Also burst capacity that allows 10% temporary headroom without instantly adding nodes.

[06:00] Priya: One question on metrics - what exact histograms do you collect so we can instrument?
[06:04] Samira: We provide token/sec, batch_size distribution, queue_depth, per-device inflight, request wait time, KV cache hit rate, and scheduler rebalance events. We'll send the Grafana dashboard link.

[06:20] Jordan: Back to the p99 spikes - Samira suggested a fallback policy: if queue depth > 800 route to a cheaper quantized variant or a cached response. Does that require extra model hosting?
[06:30] Samira: Yes you'll host the variant on the same fleet but with lower concurrency caps, or use a cold fallback with higher latency. It's a config tradeoff.

[06:45] Liam: Any notes about the sequencing of the big benchmark we're planning? Steps to reproduce?
[06:49] Jordan: We'll run a 2-hour steady-state with a 10-minute ramp, 30-minute bursts every 20 minutes to mimic traffic, collect all traces, and include the warm-up. Samira will provide the script; Priya and Liam will run it and upload artifacts.

[07:05] Marta: What about headroom for model token length? Some flows spike to 256 tokens occasionally. That affects batch depth because longer sequences take longer per request.
[07:13] Samira: Right - we factor in sequence length distribution. For occasional long sequences we recommend preserving a separate pool with higher per-request priority or different scheduling class so they don't block short flows.

[07:30] Priya: Any quick wins we can toggle today?
[07:33] Samira: Toggle 1: bump batch window to 30ms. Toggle 2: set per-device concurrency cap 12. Toggle 3: enable prefix caching and a short warm-up. Each is low-risk.

[07:50] Jordan: Okay let's call out exact numbers in next steps.

[08:00] Samira: Also, logging: include per-request batch id in logs so we can correlate which requests were in same micro-batch; that helped us debug the 14:32 event.

[08:14] Liam: On the topic of queueing, do we need a separate rate limiter in front of the runtime? We already have an API gateway rate limiter but it's coarse.
[08:24] Jordan: It's fine to use gateway for coarse rate-limiting, but the runtime's admission control should be the source of truth for backpressure. Gateway can pre-shape traffic into the desired concurrency envelope.

[08:40] Marta: Anything on cost estimates if we double the concurrency?
[08:44] Samira: Doubling concurrency without improving batching increases cost linearly; with batching improvements you get sub-linear cost increases. We'll model it in the spreadsheet and share.

[09:00] Priya: Ok we have a few follow ups - can you send the tuned config with exact flags?
[09:05] Jordan: Yes. Jordan: action items: I'll send tuned config and benchmark script; Samira will attach KMS notes and lab results; Priya and Liam will run the big benchmark next week.

[09:20] Marta: Good, but one more ask - can Redwood run a short remote run on a mirror cluster so we can compare numbers side-by-side?
[09:27] Samira: We can run a remote controlled run using your dataset if S3 and access are provided, otherwise we can run an equivalent synthetic that mimics your histograms. For best result we prefer your real prompt set.

[09:44] Jordan: Let's confirm security checklist in parallel. Marta, you had a list?
[09:47] Marta: Yes SOC2 scope and KMS rotation policies, and audit log retention. We need to confirm retention windows.

[09:55] Samira: We'll upload the SOC2 matrix and the KMS flow. Expect docs in the shared folder.

[10:05] Jordan: Alright let's recap next steps.

[10:08] Samira: Recap: toggles for immediate run (30ms window, max_batch 256, concurrency 12), Samira to send scripts and traces, Jordan to send tuned runtime config and pricing note, NovaChat to run 2-hour peak benchmark and upload artifacts, then follow-up on 2027-03-17 to review.

[10:30] Priya: Sounds good. One small note - our infra team will need the exact container image tags and helm values for the config change.
[10:37] Jordan: Will include image tags in the config.

[10:45] Marta: Thanks all, appreciate the clarity.

[10:49] Jordan: Thanks team. We'll get the artifacts over by Friday.

[11:00] (call ends)
